note: the customer with five open jobs is returned above the one with a single open job - and taking the open jobs away flips the order, which proves it is the open jobs doing it.
evidence:
Run on the test branch on 18 September 2026, build v26.36.7-29ca209, watched on screen and read from the product's own answer.

Typed ZZOPENCOUNT and opened the Customers list:
  1. ZZOPENCOUNT Freight Busy   - badge reads '5 open'
  2. ZZOPENCOUNT Freight Quiet  - badge reads '1 open'
The two records are the same in every other way - same address, same style of name, both found through the same field. Read four times in a row, identical every time.

THEN THE ORDER WAS PROVED TO BE CAUSED BY THE OPEN JOBS, not by chance. The busy customer's five jobs were closed, and the same search was run again:
  1. ZZOPENCOUNT Freight Quiet  (1 open)
  2. ZZOPENCOUNT Freight Busy   (now 0 open)
The order flipped, and the busy customer's score fell by exactly 0.20 - which is the lift the requirement gives a customer for having open work at all. Read twice, several seconds apart, to be sure the change had settled.

THE RECORDS WERE PUT BACK. Closing a job cannot be undone in the product, so five fresh jobs were created for the same customer and vehicle and set to in progress. The pair now reads 5 against 1 again, the busy customer is first again, and the full set of twenty ordering checks passes. The record of which jobs belong to this test has been updated so the next person seeding the branch is not left with the closed ones.
